source_snapshot.procedure: Enter BIOS > Advanced > Trusted Computing, check TPM version and set Security Device to Enable.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek correctly recognizes BIOS/KVM observation but substitutes unsafe SSH and truncated OS evidence, which is not the source acceptance interface.

original_test_intent.purpose: Verify on the target BIOS Trusted Computing screen that the platform displays the correct TPM information and place the Security Device option in the owner-approved Enabled state.
original_test_intent.target: The TPM information and Security Device control under BIOS > Advanced > Trusted Computing on one verified SUT/BIOS build.
original_test_intent.scope: One BIOS-setup inspection and one bounded selection of Security Device = Enable. The source does not request TPM ownership clearing, PCR operations, OS functional TPM testing or a generic tpm2-tools test.
original_test_intent.operation: Use an authorized console/KVM operator to enter the exact BIOS page, record the TPM version/information and current Security Device value, compare the displayed information with the platform recipe, and select Enable only after impact/recovery approval. Save/reboot/application verification must follow the owner clarification because the row does not define them.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: The workbook estimates 10 attended and 10 machine minutes and specifies one BIOS setup check/change.
original_test_intent.expected_result: The BIOS Trusted Computing page shows TPM information matching the approved hardware/firmware recipe and the Security Device field is set to Enable. The row does not independently define OS visibility, persistence after reboot or TPM functional behavior as acceptance criteria.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: SUT/BIOS/TPM identity and expected TPM information; before/after BIOS page captures with Security Device state; operator/action/timestamp; approval and, only if required by the owner, save/reboot and resulting state evidence; no unrelated setting-change audit.
ambiguities: The expected TPM version/information is absent.
The row does not say whether the change must be saved, rebooted and re-entered for persistence verification.
The source's generic post-test log check does not make OS TPM evidence part of acceptance.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly keeps BIOS/KVM work manual, requires approval/recovery and prohibits TPM clear. It makes OS sysfs/tpm2 evidence, saving/rebooting and recovery boot part of completion even though the source criterion only checks BIOS-displayed TPM information and sets the option. Those additions can change the test and its blast radius.

applicable_history.decision: V2 formalizes the historical PARTIAL result as REQUIRES. No later user ruling expands this exact row into an OS TPM functionality or reboot-persistence test.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Keep the hybrid/manual BIOS classification and safety controls, but restore BIOS Setup as the acceptance interface. OS TPM data may be optional corroboration only. Require the owner to resolve whether save/reboot/persistence is part of this row before the Enabled selection is committed.

available_now: The BIOS menu path, two fields of interest and desired Security Device selection are stated.
An authorized operator can collect current BIOS-screen Actual Values without committing a change once the target is verified.
missing_inputs: The BIOS/platform owner must provide the expected TPM version/information for this SUT and BIOS build.
The security/test owner must state whether Enable is only selected/displayed or must be saved, rebooted and verified for persistence, and provide impact/recovery requirements.
The lab owner must provide an authorized console/KVM operator and target-specific BIOS procedure.
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The BIOS/platform owner supplies menu/expected values; the security/test owner defines state-change, save/reboot and recovery scope; the lab owner supplies the operator and console.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Verify SUT/BIOS identity and enter the Trusted Computing page without changing values.
Capture TPM information and current Security Device state; collect optional read-only OS TPM inventory only as clearly labeled context.
prohibited_until_closed: Do not commit/save Enable, reboot, clear/reset/initialize the TPM, alter PCR/ownership/enrollment, change unrelated BIOS settings, clear logs or treat OS evidence as a substitute for the BIOS screen.
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: Receive expected TPM information and explicit save/reboot scope, confirm recovery readiness, obtain approval, capture the BIOS page before/after the bounded Enable selection, and perform only the owner-required application check.

revision_candidate.test_name: BIOS Trusted Computing TPM Information and Security Device Enable Check
revision_candidate.purpose: Verify the TPM information displayed in BIOS Trusted Computing against the platform recipe and set Security Device to the approved Enabled value without changing unrelated TPM or BIOS state.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The exact server, BIOS/UEFI build and TPM hardware/firmware combination identified by the product recipe, accessed through an authorized physical or remote KVM console.
revision_candidate.target_scope: The TPM information and Security Device option on BIOS > Advanced > Trusted Computing for one SUT. TPM clearing, ownership/PCR changes and OS functional testing are outside scope.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Verified SUT/BIOS/TPM identity; expected TPM information; target-specific menu procedure; current Security Device state; owner decision on save/reboot/persistence; impact assessment; recovery path; operator/KVM authorization; evidence storage.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: The authorized operator enters the stated BIOS page, captures the complete TPM information and current Security Device state, and compares the display with the approved recipe. After explicit approval, select Enable. Commit/save, reboot and re-entry only if the owner has defined them as part of this row. Record every action; do not use OS data to replace BIOS evidence.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Correct target and BIOS verified; expected TPM values available; console stable; no concurrent firmware/security work; change/save scope approved; encryption/measured-boot impact and recovery reviewed when a committed change is required.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Target/BIOS/TPM identity and expected values; complete before/after Trusted Computing screen captures; TPM version/information comparison; Security Device current/selected/applied state; operator, approval and timestamp; optional owner-required save/reboot evidence; unrelated-setting audit.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The owner-approved platform BIOS/TPM recipe for this exact SUT and BIOS build plus the source criterion that BIOS-displayed TPM information is correct and Security Device is set to Enable.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Do not clear/reset/initialize TPM ownership, change PCR/security policy or unrelated BIOS fields, commit/reboot without defined scope and recovery, expose console credentials, clear logs or claim BIOS state from OS-only output.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: An authorized operator performs BIOS interaction. Explicit owner approval is required before selecting/committing Enable and before any save/reboot or recovery action.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: The operator controls BIOS/KVM and certifies screen evidence. An agent may organize evidence and optional read-only corroboration, but cannot replace the BIOS visual criterion or decide the platform-specific TPM expectation.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: If an approved committed change causes a boot, encryption or state problem, stop repeated toggles, preserve BIOS/console evidence and follow the owner's documented recovery path. Never clear the TPM as an improvised recovery.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Wrong target/BIOS/menu; expected TPM value missing; ambiguous field; operator or approval absent; recovery not ready for a committed change; unrelated setting changed; unexpected encryption/boot impact; TPM clear/reset prompt; or evidence cannot prove the BIOS display and selected state.

identified_defects: DeepSeek's OS command is unsafe and not equivalent to BIOS-screen acceptance.
V2 expands the row into mandatory OS TPM functionality and save/reboot recovery without source support.
The expected TPM information and application/persistence scope are absent.
reason_for_change: Preserve the source's BIOS visual/state-change intent and strong TPM safety gates while removing mandatory OS functionality and reboot/persistence steps that the row does not request.

new_technical_evidence.title: Source testcase Wistron-HW-00367-V002
new_technical_evidence.applicability: This exact TPM BIOS Setup row
new_technical_evidence.supports: The required interface is BIOS > Advanced > Trusted Computing; the stated activities are checking TPM version/information and setting Security Device to Enable, with no OS TPM command or explicit persistence step.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Expected values and whether save/reboot/re-entry are required remain unspecified.

removed_ambiguities: Makes BIOS screen the required evidence rather than OS output.
Separates selecting Enable from an owner-defined commit/reboot/persistence test.
Excludes TPM clear, ownership, PCR and generic functional expansion.
resolved_blockers: Read-only BIOS-screen Actual Value collection can proceed before the expected TPM value and change approval are supplied.
remaining_blockers: Final comparison needs the approved TPM information.
Committing Enable needs explicit save/reboot scope, impact review, approval and recovery.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 keeps V2's safe human-controlled BIOS boundary but prevents OS corroboration, reboot and recovery-boot evidence from becoming unintended mandatory test scope.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The scope correction is queued for isolated validation at the next batch gate.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: Functionality row 1738 uses BIOS > Advanced > Trusted Computing to check TPM version and set Security Device to Enable.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 correctly gates BIOS interaction but adds mandatory OS and persistence/recovery evidence absent from the source.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Allow read-only BIOS inspection; require manual operator and approval for Enable; withhold save/reboot until owner defines it; never clear TPM.
